title: Automate CI-gated release versions
description: Automate Gateship release identity after a product pull request merges, without adding a PAT, release bot, source-version commit, second release workflow, daemon, or runtime network check. Extend the existing .github/workflows/release.yml so it still supports a manually pushed v* tag and also observes completed CI workflow runs. The automatic path must run only when the triggering CI conclusion is success, the original CI event was push, the head branch is main, and GitHub’s commit-associated-pulls API confirms that the exact head SHA is the merge commit of a merged PR into main. Direct issue/spec/approval commits and pull-request CI runs must exit successfully without tagging or publishing. Keep one release workflow: after the eligible CI result, checkout the exact head SHA, fetch tags, deterministically choose the next version using the repository’s existing pre-1.0 convention (increment the highest valid vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag’s MINOR and reset PATCH to zero), create the tag on that exact SHA, and continue in the same workflow to build and publish. Do not rely on a tag-push event created by GITHUB_TOKEN, because GitHub suppresses that recursive workflow trigger. Add concurrency and idempotency: a rerun reuses a valid version tag already pointing at the SHA; it never creates a second tag for that commit; GitHub Release asset upload is safe to repeat with replacement; manual tags remain supported. Extract version selection into a small deterministic script with tests for unsorted tags, invalid tags, no tags, and major/minor ordering. Remove the manual duplicate release literal: source/package development metadata becomes 0.0.0-dev, while native and container release builds receive and validate the semantic version derived from the exact v* tag through a compile-time define. Local/source and ordinary CI builds remain explicitly development builds. The existing --version command reports the injected release version for released binaries. The web snapshot keeps its existing version field and appends the existing workflow/build SHA as SemVer build metadata when a SHA is known, so the header identifies both release and revision without adding an endpoint or client field. Pass the same release version and build SHA to the container build. Preserve checksum generation, attestations, four native artifacts, versioned/SHA container tags, installer compatibility, and the current prerelease classification. Update focused static/behavior tests and HANDOFF.md to record automatic release identity as shipped direction. Out of scope: automatically replacing or restarting an installed binary/container, latest-release polling in the runtime, rollback/supervisor design, changelog generation, npm publication, changing provider versions, changing Gateship run lifecycle, or releasing direct administrative commits.
